survey: Stone park chess table with two stone stools on grass. Table: thick square stone top with rounded rim and inset checkerboard, seen from above at an angle; the top rests on a collar that leads into a single tapered central pedestal, which widens into a stepped square plinth sitting flat on the grass (it meets the ground and casts a shadow). Left stool: round seat (fitted ellipse ratio 0.33, 0.5% off a true ellipse, which is right for a round top seen from above) on a turned column with one ring, standing on a wider round base on the grass. Right stool: built like the left one, set further back and consistent with it. No thin parts, cables or ropes; the tool marked no ends or branches. All parts stack on the one below them and are grounded.
